claims.text: Also used for macular edema: intraocular triamcinolone or a slow-release dexamethasone implant
claims.quote: Treatment for branch retinal vein occlusion in patients with macular edema that involves the fovea is usually intraocular injection of an anti-VEGF medication (eg, ranibizumab, aflibercept, high-dose aflibercept, bevacizumab, or faricimab), intraocular injection of triamcinolone, or a slow-release dexamethasone implant (1). These treatments can also be used to treat central retinal vein occlusion in patients with macular edema.
